description: OS release identity and the Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version client hint Chromium derives from it. Windows platform versions are UniversalApiContract versions, not build numbers; macOS platform versions are OS version triples; Chromium emits an empty platform version on Linux. Each option also carries the platform's complete User-Agent string as a physical device sent it. Chrome's UA reduction freezes the OS token per platform, so the string belongs in this axis and nowhere else: one draw sets navigator.platform, both Client Hints platform reads and the UA's OS token together, and no second axis can pick a contradicting one. Its browser major is the build's, stamped in when the tables are compiled.
label: os_release

options.note: Windows 11 builds: 22000 (21H2), 22621 (22H2), 22631 (23H2), 26100 (24H2) -- the Version enum and OSInfo::MajorMinorBuildToVersion in base/win/windows_version.h. platformVersion is NOT the build number: Chromium builds the Windows Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version from the Windows.Foundation.UniversalApiContract REG_DWORD under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsRuntime\WellKnownContracts as "HIWORD.LOWORD.0", falling back to kHighestKnownUniversalApiContractVersion = 19 when the key is unreadable (components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc, GetUniversalApiContractVersion / GetWindowsPlatformVersion). 19.0.0 is measured on the Windows 11 reference host. The build number is not page-observable at all -- the UA OS token is "Windows NT 10.0" for every Windows 10 and 11 release -- so splitting 22H2/23H2/24H2 into separate options would buy no entropy and would multiply unmeasured contract claims. One Windows 11 option is the honest shape. browser.user_agent is that host's UA string verbatim; its browser major is stamped from the pinned build when the tables are compiled (scripts/profile_resolver.py:user_agent_for_build), because the version inside the UA is a build invariant and not a profile value.

browser.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

options.note: AUTHORED, NOT MEASURED. Windows 11 22H2/23H2 (builds 22621/22631). platformVersion is the UniversalApiContract version Chromium reads out of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsRuntime\WellKnownContracts and formats as "HIWORD.LOWORD.0" (components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc, GetUniversalApiContractVersion), never the build number. 19.0.0 is measured on the reference host and is also Chromium's kHighestKnownUniversalApiContractVersion, i.e. 24H2 and later. 15 is the only other contract value with a citable source, so it is the only other Windows 11 option offered; the 16/17/18 range exists in the SDK history but I found no source that maps it to a serviced Windows release, and an unsourced registry value is exactly the falsifiable kind of guess this catalogue refuses. browser.user_agent is NOT authored. The reduced UA's OS token is "Windows NT 10.0" on every serviced Windows 10 and 11 release, so the Windows UA string carries no release entropy: it is the measured string from the Windows 11 reference host, identical in all four Windows captures apart from the browser major, which is stamped from the pinned build when the tables are compiled. Only the platformVersion above is authored.
options.source: Microsoft Learn, Windows app versioning overview (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/get-started/versioning-overview): an API introduced between build 22621 and build 26100 is guarded with IsApiContractPresent("Windows.Foundation.UniversalApiContract", 15), so contract 15 is the contract present from Windows 11 22H2 (build 22621) until 24H2 raises it; resources/fingerprints/raw/windows-chrome-20260910T140813Z.json (the UA string)

browser.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

options.note: Windows 10 builds: 19041 (20H1), 19042 (20H2), 19043 (21H1), 19044 (21H2), 19045 (22H2) -- the Version enum and OSInfo::MajorMinorBuildToVersion in base/win/windows_version.h. 22H2 (19045) is the only Windows 10 release still serviced. AUTHORED, NOT MEASURED: the contract major 10 for Windows 10 2004 and later is Microsoft SDK release history, not a capture and not derivable from Chromium source. Chromium reads the value out of the registry (components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc), and the only mapping Chromium source does give is GetPreRS5UniversalApiContractVersion, which covers contract 1..6 for Windows 10 1507, 1511, 1607, 1703, 1709 and 1803 only -- all long out of service and all near-zero prevalence, so none are offered. The build number itself is not page-observable; only this contract string is. browser.user_agent is NOT authored. The reduced UA's OS token is "Windows NT 10.0" on every serviced Windows 10 and 11 release, so the Windows UA string carries no release entropy: it is the measured string from the Windows 11 reference host, identical in all four Windows captures apart from the browser major, which is stamped from the pinned build when the tables are compiled. Only the platformVersion above is authored.

options.note: GetPlatformVersion returns base::SysInfo::OperatingSystemVersionNumbers formatted "%d.%d.%d" on macOS (components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc), so the client hint is the real OS version triple. The UA string's OS token is frozen at "Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7" and carries no OS entropy. browser.user_agent is that host's UA string verbatim; its browser major is stamped from the pinned build when the tables are compiled (scripts/profile_resolver.py:user_agent_for_build), because the version inside the UA is a build invariant and not a profile value.

options.note: GetPlatformVersion returns std::string() under BUILDFLAG(IS_LINUX) (components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc), so the Linux platform version is empty by construction and carries no entropy. Measured empty on both Linux reference hosts. browser.user_agent is taken from the headed Linux workstation capture rather than the headless one cited above: a headless Chrome writes "HeadlessChrome" as its product token, which patch 0002 removes at the emitter and which no table may carry. The two captures agree on every other byte of the string. The browser major is stamped from the pinned build when the tables are compiled.
